units.zh: 太祖聖神恭肅文武孝皇帝，姓郭氏，諱威，字文仲，邢州堯山人也。
units.en: Taizu, the Sagely Divine, Respectful, Solemn, Martial, Literary, and Filial Emperor, was of the Guo clan. His personal name was Wei, his courtesy name Wenzhong, and his home was Yao Mountain in Xingzhou.
units.literal: Taizu, the Sagely Divine Respectful Solemn Martial Literary Filial Emperor, bore the surname Guo; his taboo name was Wei, his style Wenzhong, and he was a native of Yao Mountain in Xingzhou.

units.zh: 或云本常氏之子，幼隨母適郭氏，故冒其姓焉。
units.en: Some accounts hold that he was born a Chang, followed his mother into the Guo household as a child, and thereafter bore the Guo surname.
units.literal: Some say he was originally a son of the Chang clan; in youth he followed his mother in marrying into the Guo clan, and therefore took their surname.

units.zh: 〈（《五代會要》：周虢叔之後。）〉
units.en: (According to the Institutional Compendium of the Five Dynasties, the house descended from Guo Shu of Zhou.)
units.literal: (From the "Institutional Compendium of the Five Dynasties": a descendant of Guo Shu of Zhou.)

units.zh: 高祖諱璟，廣順初，追尊為睿和皇帝，廟號信祖，陵曰溫陵；
units.en: The high ancestor, taboo name Jing, was posthumously enthroned as Emperor Ruihe at the opening of Guangshun, with the temple name Xizu and the mausoleum Wenling;
units.literal: The High Ancestor's taboo name was Jing; at the beginning of the Guangshun era he was posthumously honored as Emperor Ruihe, with temple name Xizu and mausoleum called Wenling;

units.zh: 高祖妣張氏，追謚睿恭皇后。
units.en: The High Ancestor's consort, Lady Zhang, received the posthumous title Empress Ruigong.
units.literal: The High Ancestor's consort, née Zhang, was posthumously given the title Empress Ruigong.

units.zh: 曾祖諱諶，漢贈太保，追尊為明憲皇帝，廟號僖祖，陵曰齊陵；
units.en: The great-grandfather, taboo name Chen, was made Grand Guardian under the Han and later raised to Emperor Mingxian, with the temple name Xizu and the mausoleum Qiling;
units.literal: The great-grandfather's taboo name was Chen; the Han posthumously made him Grand Guardian, and he was later honored as Emperor Mingxian, with temple name Xizu and mausoleum Qiling;

units.zh: 曾祖妣鄭國夫人申氏，追謚明孝皇后。
units.en: Lady Shen of Zheng was posthumously styled Empress Mingxiao.
units.literal: The great-grandmother, Lady Shen, Lady of Zheng, was posthumously given the title Empress Mingxiao.

units.zh: 祖諱蘊，漢贈太傅，追尊為翼順皇帝，廟號義祖，陵曰節陵；
units.en: The grandfather, taboo name Yun, was made Grand Tutor under the Han and later raised to Emperor Yishun, with the temple name Yizu and the mausoleum Jieling;
units.literal: The grandfather's taboo name was Yun; the Han posthumously made him Grand Tutor, and he was later honored as Emperor Yishun, with temple name Yizu and mausoleum Jieling;

units.zh: 〈（《五代會要》：溫陵、齊陵、節陵皆無陵所，遙申朝拜。）〉
units.en: (The Institutional Compendium notes that Wenling, Qiling, and Jieling had no physical burial sites; rites were performed by distant petition.)
units.literal: (From the "Institutional Compendium of the Five Dynasties": Wenling, Qiling, and Jieling all had no actual tomb sites; worship was offered from afar.)

units.zh: 祖妣陳國夫人韓氏，追謚翼敬皇后。
units.en: Lady Han of Chen received the posthumous title Empress Yijing.
units.literal: The grandmother, Lady Han, Lady of Chen, was posthumously given the title Empress Yijing.

units.zh: 皇考諱簡，漢贈太師，追尊為章肅皇帝，廟號慶祖，陵曰欽陵；
units.en: His father, taboo name Jian, was made Grand Preceptor under the Han and later raised to Emperor Zhangsu, with the temple name Qingzu and the mausoleum Qinling;
units.literal: The Imperial Father's taboo name was Jian; the Han posthumously made him Grand Preceptor, and he was later honored as Emperor Zhangsu, with temple name Qingzu and mausoleum Qinling;

units.zh: 皇妣燕國夫人王氏，追謚為章德皇后。
units.en: His mother, Lady Wang of Yan, was posthumously styled Empress Zhangde.
units.literal: The Imperial Mother, Lady Wang, Lady of Yan, was posthumously given the title Empress Zhangde.

units.zh: 後以唐天祐元年甲子歲七月二十八日，生帝於堯山之舊宅。
units.en: On the twenty-eighth day of the seventh month in the first Tianyou year of Tang (jiazi), he was born at the family's old home on Yao Mountain.
units.literal: Later, on the twenty-eighth day of the seventh month in the first year of Tianyou of Tang, the year jiazi, the Emperor was born at the old residence on Yao Mountain.

units.zh: 載誕之夕，赤光照室，有聲如爐炭之裂，星火四迸。
units.en: On the night he was born, a crimson glow filled the room, charcoal seemed to crackle in the brazier, and sparks burst outward on every side.
units.literal: On the night of his birth, red light filled the chamber; there was a sound like charcoal splitting in a brazier, and sparks flew in all directions.

units.zh: 帝生三歲，家徙太原。
units.en: At the age of three he moved with his family to Taiyuan.
units.literal: When the Emperor was three years old, the family moved to Taiyuan.

units.zh: 居無何，皇考為燕軍所陷，歿於王事。
units.en: Before long his father was cut off by the Yan forces and died in the king's service.
units.literal: Before long, the Imperial Father was trapped by the Yan army and died in the service of the state.

units.zh: 帝未及齠齔，章德太后蚤世，姨母楚國夫人韓氏提攜鞠養。
units.en: He was still a small child when Empress Zhangde died. His aunt, Lady Han of Chu, took him in and raised him.
units.literal: The Emperor had not yet reached childhood; Empress Dowager Zhangde died early, and his aunt, Lady Han, Lady of Chu, took him in hand and reared him.

units.zh: 及長，形神魁壯，趨向奇崛，愛兵好勇，不事田產。
units.en: As he matured he grew tall and powerfully built, with an uncommon bearing. He loved arms and prized courage and cared nothing for farming.
units.literal: When he grew up, his form and spirit were towering and strong, his bent extraordinary and lofty; he loved soldiers and delighted in valor, and did not engage in farming.

units.zh: 天祐末，潞州節度使李嗣昭常山戰歿，子繼韜自稱留後，南結梁朝，據城阻命，乃散金以募豪傑。
units.en: Late in the Tianyou era Li Sizhao, governor of Luzhou, fell at Changshan. His son Jitao declared himself acting governor, sought Liang support in the south, held the city against orders, and scattered gold to recruit daring men.
units.literal: At the end of Tianyou, Li Sizhao, military governor of Luzhou, was killed in battle at Changshan; his son Jitao styled himself acting governor, allied with the Liang to the south, held the city in defiance of orders, and scattered gold to recruit bold men.

units.zh: 帝時年十八，避吏壺關，依故人常氏，遂往應募。
units.en: He was eighteen at the time, dodging the authorities at Huguan while staying with his old friend the Changs, and then went to enlist.
units.literal: The Emperor was then eighteen; evading the officials at Huguan, he relied on his old acquaintance the Chang clan and thereupon went to answer the recruitment.

units.zh: 帝負氣用剛，好鬥多力，繼韜奇之，或逾法犯禁，亦多假借焉。
units.en: Proud and unyielding, he loved a fight and had uncommon strength. Jitao took him for a remarkable man and often overlooked his breaches of law and discipline.
units.literal: The Emperor was proud in spirit and firm in conduct, fond of fighting and possessed of great strength; Jitao regarded him as extraordinary, and even when he overstepped the law and violated prohibitions, he often indulged him.

units.zh: 嘗遊上黨市，有市屠壯健，眾所畏憚，帝以氣淩之，因醉命屠割肉，小不如意，叱之。
units.en: Once in the Shangdang market he came upon a butcher so burly that everyone feared him. He lorded it over the man and, drunk, ordered him to carve meat; when the cuts were not quite right he shouted at him.
units.literal: Once when he was strolling through the market at Shangdang, there was a butcher in the market, stout and strong, whom all feared; the Emperor overawed him with his spirit, and while drunk ordered the butcher to slice meat; when it was slightly not to his liking, he berated him.

units.zh: 屠者怒，坦腹謂帝曰：「爾敢刺我否？」
units.en: The butcher flew into a rage, bared his belly, and said to him, "Think you can stab me?"
units.literal: The butcher in anger, baring his belly, said to the Emperor: "Do you dare stab me or not?"

units.zh: 帝即事刂其腹，市人執之屬吏，繼韜惜而逸之。
units.en: Without hesitation he drove a blade into the man's belly. The crowd seized him and turned him over to the authorities, but Jitao valued him and let him go.
units.literal: The Emperor at once stabbed his belly; the people of the market seized him and handed him over to the officials; Jitao prized him and released him.

units.zh: 其年，莊宗平梁，繼韜伏誅，麾下牙兵配從馬直，帝在籍中，時年二十一。
units.en: That year Zhuangzong conquered Liang. Jitao was put to death and his personal troops were assigned to the Imperial Horse Escort, with Guo Wei on the rolls at the age of twenty-one.
units.literal: That year Zhuangzong pacified Liang; Jitao was executed, and the yak troops under his command were assigned to the Imperial Horse Escort; the Emperor was on the rolls, aged twenty-one.

units.zh: 帝性聰敏，喜筆劄，及從軍旅，多閱簿書，軍誌戎政，深窮綮肯，人皆服其敏。
units.en: Quick-witted by nature, he loved letters. Once in the ranks he pored over ledgers and registers and mastered military affairs down to their roots, and everyone marveled at his acuity.
units.literal: The Emperor by nature was clever and keen, fond of writing; when he joined the army he read many ledgers and registers, and in military records and martial administration he thoroughly mastered the essentials, and all admired his quickness.

units.zh: 嘗省昭義李瓊，瓊方讀《閫外春秋》，即取視之，曰：「論兵也，兄其教我。」
units.en: Once he called on Li Qiong of Zhaoyi, who was reading the Springs and Autumns Outside the Gate. He took the book and said, "This is about war, brother — teach me."
units.literal: Once when he called on Li Qiong of Zhaoyi, Qiong was just reading the "Springs and Autumns Outside the Gate"; he took it at once to look at it and said: "This discusses warfare; elder brother, please teach me."

units.zh: 即授之，深通義理。
units.en: Qiong gave him the book, and he came to a deep grasp of its doctrines.
units.literal: He at once handed it to him, and he thoroughly penetrated its principles.

units.zh: 〈（《宋史·李瓊傳》：唐莊宗慕勇士，即應募，與周祖等十人約為兄弟。
units.en: (From Li Qiong's biography in the History of Song: Zhuangzong of Tang sought bold warriors. Guo Wei enlisted and, with nine companions including Li Qiong, swore brotherhood.
units.literal: (From the "Biography of Li Qiong" in the History of Song: Tang Zhuangzong admired brave warriors; he at once answered the recruitment and with the Zhou Ancestor and nine others pledged brotherhood.

units.zh: 一日會飲，瓊熟視周祖，知非常人，因舉酒祝曰：「凡我十人，尤蛇混合，異日富貴，無相忘。
units.en: One day over wine Qiong studied Guo Wei closely and knew he was no ordinary man. He raised his cup and said, "We ten, noble and humble alike — when fortune comes, let none forget the rest.
units.literal: One day at a drinking gathering Qiong studied the Zhou Ancestor closely, knew he was no ordinary man, and thereupon raised his cup in a toast, saying: "All we ten, high and low mingled together, when one day we are rich and noble, let none forget the rest.

units.zh: 苛渝此言，神降之罰。」
units.en: Whoever breaks this oath, let the spirits punish him."
units.literal: If anyone violates this vow, may the spirits descend punishment."

units.zh: 皆刺臂出血為誓。
units.en: They all pricked their arms and sealed the vow in blood.
units.literal: All pricked their arms and drew blood as oath.

units.zh: 周祖與瓊情好尤密，嘗造瓊，見其危坐讀書，因問所讀何書，瓊曰：「此《閫外春秋》，所謂以正守國，以奇用兵，較存亡治亂，記賢愚成敗，皆在此也。」
units.en: Guo Wei and Qiong were especially close. Once he called on Qiong and found him reading upright. Asked what book it was, Qiong said, "This is the Springs and Autumns Outside the Gate — to hold a state by rectitude, to fight by stratagem, to weigh survival and ruin, order and chaos, and to record who won or lost, the wise and the foolish — all of that is here."
units.literal: The Zhou Ancestor and Qiong were especially close in affection; once he visited Qiong and saw him sitting upright reading a book, and therefore asked what book he was reading; Qiong said: "This is the 'Springs and Autumns Outside the Gate' — what is called using rectitude to guard the state and using the unexpected in employing troops, comparing survival and extinction, order and disorder, recording the worthy and the foolish, success and failure — all are in this."

units.zh: 周祖令讀之，謂瓊曰：「兄當教我。」
units.en: Guo Wei had him read it and said, "Brother, you must teach me."
units.literal: The Zhou Ancestor had him read it and said to Qiong: "Elder brother ought to teach me."

units.zh: 自是周祖出入，常袖以自隨，遇暇輒讀，每問難瓊，謂瓊為師。）〉
units.en: Thereafter he carried the book in his sleeve whenever he went abroad, read it whenever he had a spare moment, questioned Qiong constantly, and called Qiong his teacher.) (End of editorial note.)〉
units.literal: From then on, whenever the Zhou Ancestor went out or in, he always kept it in his sleeve; when he had leisure he would read it, and whenever he questioned Qiong he called Qiong his teacher.) (End of editorial note.)〉

units.zh: 天成初，明宗幸浚郊。
units.en: Early in the Tiancheng era Emperor Mingzong toured the Jun suburbs.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng, Mingzong visited the suburbs of Jun.

units.zh: 時朱守殷嬰城拒命，帝從晉高祖一軍率先登城。
units.en: Zhu Shouyin was then holding the city against orders. Guo Wei followed the army of the future Jin Gaozu and was first over the wall.
units.literal: At that time Zhu Shouyin held the city in defiance of orders; the Emperor followed the Jin High Ancestor's army and was first to scale the wall.

units.zh: 晉祖領副侍衛，以帝長於書計，召置麾下，令掌軍籍，前後將臣，無不倚愛。
units.en: The future Jin Gaozu was deputy commander of the Imperial Guard. Seeing Guo Wei's skill with accounts, he took him into his service to manage the rolls, and every officer came to rely on and favor him.
units.literal: The Jin Ancestor held the post of deputy commander of the Imperial Guard; because the Emperor excelled at writing and reckoning, he summoned him and placed him under his banner, ordering him to manage the military rolls; generals and ministers before and after all relied on and loved him.

units.zh: 初，聖穆皇后嬪於帝，帝方匱乏，而後多資從。
units.en: Early on Empress Shengmu became his consort while he was still poor; she often supplied him with funds and goods.
units.literal: At first the Sagely Solemn Empress was a consort of the Emperor; the Emperor was then in want, while the Empress often supplied him with resources.

units.zh: 〈（《東都事略》：柴後資周太祖以金帛，使事漢高祖。）〉
units.en: (The Summary of Affairs in the Eastern Capital records that Lady Chai furnished Guo Wei with gold and silks so he could enter the service of the future Han Gaozu.)
units.literal: (From the "Summary of Affairs in the Eastern Capital": the Empress Chai supplied the Zhou Taizu with gold and silks so that he might serve the Han High Ancestor.)

units.zh: 帝嘗晝寢，有小虺五色，出入顴鼻之間，後遽見愕然。
units.en: Once while he napped by day a small five-colored serpent moved between his temples and nose. The empress saw it and was struck with awe.
units.literal: The Emperor once slept by day; a small serpent of five colors went in and out between his temples and nose; the Empress suddenly saw it and was startled.

units.zh: 在太原時，有神尼與帝同姓，見帝，謂李瓊曰：「我宗天上大仙，頂上有肉角，當為世界主。」
units.en: At Taiyuan a nun of his own surname saw him and told Li Qiong, "A great immortal of our house walks the earth — there is a fleshy horn on his crown, and he is destined to rule the world."
units.literal: When he was at Taiyuan, there was a divine nun of the same surname as the Emperor; seeing the Emperor, she said to Li Qiong: "Our clan's great immortal of heaven has a fleshy horn on his crown and ought to become lord of the world."

units.zh: 清泰末，晉祖起於河東，時河陽節度使張彥琪為侍衛步軍都指揮使，奉命北伐，帝從之，營於晉祠。
units.en: Late in Qingtai the future Jin Gaozu rose in Hedong. Zhang Yanqi of Heyang, then commander of the guard infantry, was ordered north on campaign, and Guo Wei went with him, encamping at the Jin Shrine.
units.literal: At the end of Qingtai the Jin Ancestor rose in Hedong; at that time Zhang Yanqi, military governor of Heyang, was commander of the infantry of the Imperial Guard and, ordered to campaign north, the Emperor followed him and encamped at the Jin Shrine.

units.zh: 是時屋壞，同處數人俱斃，唯帝獨無所傷。
units.en: Then a building collapsed and killed several men who were inside with him, but he alone escaped injury.
units.literal: At that time a building collapsed; several men who were in the same place were all killed, but the Emperor alone was unharmed.

units.zh: 漢高祖為侍衛馬步都虞候，召置左右。
units.en: When the future Han Gaozu became commander of the guard cavalry and infantry, he summoned Guo Wei to his side.
units.literal: The Han High Ancestor was commander of the horse and foot of the Imperial Guard and summoned him to place him at his side.

units.zh: 所居官舍之鄰吳氏，有青衣佳娘者，為山魈所魅，鬼能人言而投瓦石，鄰伍無敢過吳氏之舍者。
units.en: Beside his quarters lived the Wus, whose young maid in blue had been possessed by a mountain demon. The spirit spoke like a man and hurled tiles and stones, and none of the neighbors dared pass their door.
units.literal: Next to the official quarters where he dwelt was the Wu household; there was a fine young woman in blue garments whom a mountain sprite had bewitched; the ghost could speak like a man and throw tiles and stones, and none of the neighbors dared pass the Wu dwelling.

units.zh: 帝過之，其鬼寂然，帝去如故，如是者再。
units.en: When he passed by, the ghost fell silent; when he left, it raged again. This happened twice.
units.literal: When the Emperor passed by, the ghost fell silent; when the Emperor left, it was as before — this happened twice.

units.zh: 或謂鬼曰：「爾既神，向者客來，又何寂然？」
units.en: Someone asked the spirit, "If you are so powerful, why did you fall silent when that guest came?"
units.literal: Someone said to the ghost: "Since you are divine, when that guest came just now, why were you so silent?"

units.zh: 鬼曰：「彼大人者。」
units.en: The spirit answered, "That was a great man."
units.literal: The ghost said: "That is a great man."

units.zh: 繇是軍中異之。
units.en: From then on the army looked on him as someone out of the ordinary.
units.literal: From this the army regarded him as extraordinary.

units.zh: 範延光叛於魏，命楊光遠討之，帝當行，意不願從。
units.en: When Fan Yanguang rebelled in Wei, Yang Guangyuan was ordered against him. Guo Wei was to accompany the campaign but did not wish to go.
units.literal: Fan Yanguang rebelled in Wei; Yang Guangyuan was ordered to suppress him; the Emperor was to go but was unwilling to follow.

units.zh: 或謂帝曰：「楊公當朝重勛，子不欲從，何也？」
units.en: Someone asked him, "Lord Yang is one of the court's greatest men of merit — why will you not follow him?"
units.literal: Someone said to the Emperor: "Lord Yang is a great meritorious minister of the court; you do not wish to follow him — why?"

units.zh: 帝曰：「楊公素無英雄氣，得我何用？
units.en: He replied, "Yang has no heroic spirit. What use would he make of me?
units.literal: The Emperor said: "Lord Yang by nature has no heroic spirit; what use would he have for me?

units.zh: 能用我其劉公乎！」
units.en: The man who could use me is Lord Liu!"
units.literal: The one who could use me would be Lord Liu!"

units.zh: 漢祖累鎮藩閫，皆從之。
units.en: Liu repeatedly governed frontier provinces, and Guo Wei always followed him.
units.literal: The Han Ancestor repeatedly governed frontier provinces, and he always followed him.

units.zh: 及鎮並門，尤深待遇，出入帷幄，受腹心之寄，帝亦悉心竭力，知無不為。
units.en: When Liu governed Bingzhou he treated Guo Wei with exceptional favor, taking him in and out of his council tent and entrusting him with his innermost designs. Guo Wei in turn gave his utmost and left nothing undone.
units.literal: When he governed Bingmen he was treated with especial depth; entering and leaving the command tent, he received the trust of innermost counsel; the Emperor also devoted his heart and strength, and there was nothing he knew of that he did not do.

units.zh: 及吐渾白可久叛入契丹，帝勸漢祖誅白承福等五族，得良馬數千匹、財貨百萬計以資軍。
units.en: When the Tuhun leader Bai Kejiu defected to the Khitan, he urged Liu to execute the five Bai clans including Chengfu, securing several thousand fine horses and wealth in the millions for the army.
units.literal: When the Tuhun Bai Kejiu rebelled and entered the Khitan, the Emperor urged the Han Ancestor to execute the five clans including Bai Chengfu, obtaining several thousand fine horses and wealth reckoned in the millions to supply the army.

units.zh: 開運末，契丹入汴，晉帝北遷。
units.en: Late in the Kaiyun era the Khitan entered Bianliang and the Jin emperor was carried north.
units.literal: At the end of Kaiyun the Khitan entered Bian, and the Jin Emperor moved north.

units.zh: 帝與蘇逢吉、楊邠、史宏肇等勸漢祖建號，以副人望。
units.en: He joined Su Fengji, Yang Bin, Shi Hongzhao, and others in urging Liu to take the throne and answer the people's hopes.
units.literal: The Emperor, with Su Fengji, Yang Bin, Shi Hongzhao, and others, urged the Han Ancestor to establish a reign title to answer the people's hopes.

units.zh: 漢高祖即位晉陽，時百度草創，四方猶梗，經綸締構，帝有力焉。
units.en: When Han Gaozu was enthroned at Jinyang the realm was still being built from nothing and the provinces remained unsettled; Guo Wei played a major part in shaping the new order.
units.literal: When the Han High Ancestor took the throne at Jinyang, at that time the hundred affairs were newly founded and the four quarters still obstructed; in planning and founding the state the Emperor had strength in it.

units.zh: 授權樞密副使、檢校司徒。
units.en: He was made acting Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Acting Minister of Education.
units.literal: He was given acting appointment as Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Acting Minister of Education.

units.zh: 漢高祖至汴，正授樞密副使、檢校太保。
units.en: When Han Gaozu reached Bianliang he received formal appointment as Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Acting Grand Guardian.
units.literal: When the Han High Ancestor reached Bian, he was formally appointed Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Acting Grand Guardian.

units.zh: 乾祐元年春，漢高祖不豫，及大漸，與蘇逢吉等同受顧命。
units.en: In the spring of the first Qianyou year Han Gaozu fell ill; as his end approached he, with Su Fengji and others, received the dying charge.
units.literal: In spring of the first year of Qianyou the Han High Ancestor was unwell, and as his illness deepened he, with Su Fengji and others, together received the dying charge.

units.zh: 隱帝嗣位，拜樞密使，加檢校太尉。
units.en: When Emperor Yin succeeded, Guo Wei was made Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs with the additional title Acting Grand Commandant.
units.literal: When the Hidden Emperor succeeded, he was made Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and given the additional title of Acting Grand Commandant.

units.zh: 舊制，樞密使未加使相者，不宣麻制，至是宣之，自帝始也。
units.en: By old custom a commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs who had not also been made a chief councilor was not announced by hemp edict; from Guo Wei onward that changed.
units.literal: By old regulation, a Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs who had not been given the status of commissioner with ministerial powers did not have hemp edicts proclaimed; at this time it was proclaimed, beginning with the Emperor.

units.zh: 〈（《東都事略魏仁浦傳》：仁溥少為刀筆吏，隸樞密院，太祖問以卒乘數，仁溥對曰：「帶甲者六萬。」
units.en: (From Wei Renpu's biography in the Summary of Affairs in the Eastern Capital: In youth Renpu was a clerk in the Bureau of Military Affairs. Taizu asked how many troops he had, and Renpu answered, "Sixty thousand under arms."
units.literal: (From the "Biography of Wei Renpu" in the Summary of Affairs in the Eastern Capital: Renpu in youth was a clerk with brush and knife, attached to the Bureau of Military Affairs; the Taizu asked him the number of soldiers and chariots, and Renpu replied: "Those in armor are sixty thousand."

units.zh: 太祖喜曰：「天下事不足憂也。」）〉
units.en: Taizu was delighted and said, "There is nothing under heaven worth worrying about."
units.literal: The Taizu rejoiced and said: "Affairs under heaven are not worth worrying over."

units.zh: 有頃，河中李守貞據城反，朝廷憂之，諸大臣共議進取之計。
units.en: Before long Li Shouzhen of Hezhong rebelled and held the city. The court was alarmed, and the chief ministers debated how to take him.
units.literal: Before long Li Shouzhen of Hezhong held the city in rebellion; the court was troubled, and the great ministers together discussed plans for advancing to take it.

units.zh: 史宏肇曰：「守貞，河陽一客司耳，竟何能為？」
units.en: Shi Hongzhao said, "Shouzhen is only a staff officer from Heyang — what can he really do?"
units.literal: Shi Hongzhao said: "Shouzhen is only a guest officer of Heyang — what can he ultimately do?"

units.zh: 帝曰：「守貞雖不習戎行，然善接英豪，得人死力，亦敵，宜審料之。」
units.en: Guo Wei said, "Shouzhen may not be a soldier by training, but he wins heroes to his side and commands their utmost loyalty. He is a foe to be reckoned with."
units.literal: The Emperor said: "Although Shouzhen is not practiced in military affairs, yet he is good at receiving heroic men and wins men's strength unto death; he is also an adversary and ought to be carefully weighed."

units.zh: 乃命白文珂、常思率兵攻取。
units.en: He then ordered Bai Wenke and Chang Si to lead troops against him.
units.literal: He thereupon ordered Bai Wenke and Chang Si to lead troops to attack and take it.

units.zh: 師未至，而趙思綰竊據永興，王景崇反狀亦露，朝廷遣郭從義、王峻討趙思綰。
units.en: Before the army arrived, Zhao Sizhen seized Yongxing and Wang Jingchong's rebellion came to light. The court sent Guo Congyi and Wang Jun against Zhao.
units.literal: The army had not yet arrived when Zhao Sizhen secretly seized Yongxing; Wang Jingchong's signs of rebellion also appeared, and the court sent Guo Congyi and Wang Jun against Zhao Sizhen.

units.zh: 七月，西面師徒大集，未果進取。
units.en: In the seventh month the western armies massed but made no advance.
units.literal: In the seventh month the western armies gathered in great numbers but did not succeed in advancing to take.

units.zh: 其月十三日，制授帝同平章事，即遣西征，以安慰招撫為名，詔西面諸軍，並取帝節度。
units.en: On the thirteenth of that month he was made Associate Councilor of State and sent west on campaign, nominally to reassure and win over the region. An edict placed all western armies under his command.
units.literal: On the thirteenth day of that month, by edict he was made Associate Councilor of State and at once sent on the western campaign, under the name of comforting and winning over; an edict to all the western armies ordered that they all take his command.

units.zh: 時論以白文珂、常思非守貞之敵，聞帝西行，群情大愜。
units.en: Public opinion held that Bai Wenke and Chang Si were no match for Shouzhen; when word spread that Guo Wei was marching west, morale rose sharply.
units.literal: Contemporary opinion held that Bai Wenke and Chang Si were no match for Shouzhen; when they heard the Emperor was going west, public sentiment was greatly satisfied.

units.zh: 〈（《宋史·李蒨傳》：周祖討河中，蒨掌轉運。
units.en: (From Li Qian's biography in the History of Song: When Guo Wei campaigned against Hezhong, Qian directed transport.
units.literal: (From the "Biography of Li Qian" in the History of Song: the Zhou Ancestor campaigned against Hezhong, and Qian was in charge of transport.

units.zh: 時周祖已有人望，潛貯異志，屢以諷蒨，蒨但對以人臣當盡節奉上而已。）〉
units.en: Guo Wei already enjoyed wide esteem and secretly harbored larger ambitions. He repeatedly sounded Qian out, but Qian would only say that a subject must serve his sovereign with full loyalty.
units.literal: At that time the Zhou Ancestor already had the people's regard and secretly harbored other designs; he repeatedly hinted to Qian, but Qian only answered that a subject ought to exhaust his loyalty in serving the sovereign.

units.zh: 八月六日，帝發離京師。
units.en: On the sixth day of the eighth month he departed the capital.
units.literal: On the sixth day of the eighth month the Emperor set out from the capital.

units.zh: 二十日，師至河中。
units.en: On the twentieth the army reached Hezhong.
units.literal: On the twentieth day the army reached Hezhong.

units.zh: 〈（《宋史·扈彥珂傳》：周祖為樞密使，總兵出征，時議多以先討景崇、思綰為便，周祖意未決。
units.en: (From Hu Yanke's biography in the History of Song: As commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Guo Wei commanded the expedition. Many argued that Jingchong and Sizhen should be struck first, but he had not yet decided.
units.literal: (From the "Biography of Hu Yanke" in the History of Song: the Zhou Ancestor was Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and commanded the army on campaign; contemporary opinion mostly held that attacking Jingchong and Sizhen first would be advantageous, but the Zhou Ancestor's mind was not yet decided.

units.zh: 彥珂曰：「三叛連衡，推守貞為主，宜先擊河中。
units.en: Yanke said, "The three rebels are allied and take Shouzhen as their head. We should strike Hezhong first.
units.literal: Yanke said: "The three rebels are allied in league and make Shouzhen their leader; one ought first to strike Hezhong.

units.zh: 河中平，則永興、鳳翔失勢矣。
units.en: Once Hezhong falls, Yongxing and Fengxiang will lose their leverage.
units.literal: If Hezhong is pacified, then Yongxing and Fengxiang will lose their strength.

units.zh: 今舍近圖遠，若景崇、思綰逆戰於前，守貞兵其後，腹背受敵，為之奈何？」
units.en: If we leave the near foe for the distant one and Jingchong and Sizhen fight us in front while Shouzhen strikes from behind, we will be caught between two fires. What then?"
units.literal: Now if we abandon what is near to aim at what is far, should Jingchong and Sizhen meet us in battle in front and Shouzhen's troops come behind, we would be attacked front and rear — what then could be done?"

units.zh: 周祖從其言。）〉
units.en: Guo Wei followed his advice.
units.literal: The Zhou Ancestor followed his words.

units.zh: 命白文珂營於河西，帝營於河東。
units.en: Bai Wenke was ordered to camp on the west bank of the river and Guo Wei on the east.
units.literal: He ordered Bai Wenke to encamp on the west bank of the river and the Emperor to encamp on the east bank.

units.zh: 不數日，周設長塹，復築長連城以迫之。
units.en: Within days they threw up long trenches and built a chain of linked walls to press the siege.
units.literal: Within a few days they laid long trenches around the city and also built a long chain of linked walls to press upon it.

units.zh: 帝在軍，居常接賓客，與大將宴語，即褒衣博帶；
units.en: In camp he regularly received guests and, when feasting with his generals, wore loose robes with broad belts;
units.literal: When the Emperor was in the army, he ordinarily received guests; when feasting and conversing with great generals, he wore loose robes with broad belts;

units.zh: 或遇巡城壘，對陳敵，幅巾短後，與眾無殊。
units.en: but when he inspected the walls or faced the enemy in battle line he wore a plain headcloth and short jacket like any common soldier.
units.literal: or when he went on rounds of the walls and ramparts facing the enemy in battle array, he wore a headcloth and short jacket at the rear, no different from the multitude.

units.zh: 臨矢石，冒鋒刃，必以身先，與士伍分甘共苦。
units.en: Under arrow and blade he always led from the front and shared hardship and comfort with the men.
units.literal: Facing arrows and stones, braving blades, he always took the lead in person and shared sweetness and bitterness with the rank and file.

units.zh: 稍立功效者，厚其賜與；
units.en: Those who achieved even modest success received generous rewards;
units.literal: Those who had achieved even slight merit, he richly rewarded;

units.zh: 微有傷痍者，親為循撫。
units.en: those with even slight wounds he comforted in person.
units.literal: those with even slight wounds, he personally went to comfort.

units.zh: 士無賢不肖，有所陳啟，溫顏以接，俾盡其情，人之過忤，未嘗介意，故君子小人皆思效用。
units.en: Whether worthy or base, any soldier who wished to speak was met with a kindly face and heard to the full. He never bore a grudge when men crossed him, and so both the upright and the rough were eager to serve him.
units.literal: Soldiers whether worthy or base, if they had something to present or report, he received them with a gentle countenance and let them fully express themselves; if men offended or crossed him, he never took it to heart, and therefore gentlemen and petty men alike wished to serve him with effort.

units.zh: 守貞聞之，深以為憂。
units.en: When Shouzhen heard of this, he was deeply alarmed.
units.literal: When Shouzhen heard of this, he was deeply troubled.

units.zh: 十二月，帝以蜀軍屯大散關，即親率牙兵往鳳翔、永興。
units.en: In the twelfth month, learning that Shu troops were at Dasanguan, he personally led his guard toward Fengxiang and Yongxing.
units.literal: In the twelfth month, because Shu troops were encamped at Dasanguan, the Emperor at once personally led his personal troops toward Fengxiang and Yongxing.

units.zh: 相度將發，謂白文珂、劉詞曰：「困獸猶鬥，當謹備之。」
units.en: As he prepared to march, he told Bai Wenke and Liu Ci, "A cornered beast still fights. We must stay on our guard."
units.literal: As he surveyed and was about to set out, he said to Bai Wenke and Liu Ci: "A cornered beast still fights — one must guard against it carefully."

units.zh: 帝至華州，聞蜀軍退敗，遂還。
units.en: He reached Huazhou, heard that the Shu army had been beaten back, and returned.
units.literal: When the Emperor reached Huazhou and heard the Shu army had retreated in defeat, he then returned.

units.zh: 二年正月五日夜，李守貞遣將王三鐵領千餘人，夜突河西呰，果為劉詞等力戰敗之。
units.en: On the night of the fifth day of the first month in the second year, Li Shouzhen sent Wang Santie with more than a thousand men in a night raid on the west-bank stockade. Liu Ci and others met them in fierce fighting and drove them off.
units.literal: On the night of the fifth day of the first month of the second year, Li Shouzhen sent the general Wang Santie leading more than a thousand men in a night assault on the west-bank stockade; they were indeed defeated in fierce fighting by Liu Ci and others.

units.zh: 先是，軍中禁酒，帝有愛將李審犯令，斬之以徇。
units.en: Earlier the army had forbidden wine. When his favorite officer Li Shen broke the rule, he beheaded him as an example.
units.literal: Earlier, wine was forbidden in the army; the Emperor had a beloved officer Li Shen who violated the order, and he beheaded him to display as warning.

units.zh: 五月九日，取河西寨，賊將周光遜以寨及部眾千餘人來降。
units.en: On the ninth day of the fifth month they captured the west-bank stockade. The rebel general Zhou Guangxun surrendered the post and more than a thousand men.
units.literal: On the ninth day of the fifth month they took the west-bank stockade; the rebel general Zhou Guangxun surrendered the stockade and more than a thousand of his troops.

units.zh: 十七日，下令攻城，會西北大風，揚沙晦冥，帝令禱河伯祠，奠訖而風止，自是晝夜攻之。
units.en: On the seventeenth he ordered the assault. A fierce northwest wind whipped up sand and darkened the sky. He had prayers offered at the River Lord shrine, and when the rites were finished the wind died. Thereafter the attack continued day and night.
units.literal: On the seventeenth day he ordered an assault on the city; a great northwest wind arose, whirling sand and darkening the sky; the Emperor ordered prayers at the River Lord shrine, and when the offerings were completed the wind stopped; from then on they attacked day and night.

units.zh: 七月十三日，帝率三寨將士奪賊羅城。
units.en: On the thirteenth day of the seventh month he led the troops of the three camps in taking the rebels' outer wall.
units.literal: On the thirteenth day of the seventh month the Emperor led the troops of the three camps to seize the rebels' outer wall.

units.zh: 二十一日，城陷，守貞舉家自焚而死。
units.en: On the twenty-first the city fell. Shouzhen and his entire household burned themselves to death.
units.literal: On the twenty-first day the city fell; Shouzhen and his whole household burned themselves to death.

units.zh: 帝前夢河神告曰：「七月下旬，上帝當滅守貞之族。」
units.en: He had earlier dreamed that the River God told him, "In the latter part of the seventh month Heaven will destroy Shouzhen's house."
units.literal: Earlier the Emperor had dreamed that the River God told him: "In the latter part of the seventh month the Supreme Lord will destroy Shouzhen's clan."

units.zh: 至是收復賊壘，城中人言，見帝營上有紫氣，如樓閣華蓋之狀。
units.en: When the rebel stronghold was recovered, people in the city said they saw purple vapor above his camp, shaped like towers and a ceremonial canopy.
units.literal: When they had recovered the rebel fort, people in the city said they saw purple vapor above the Emperor's camp, like towers and a ceremonial canopy.

units.zh: 〈（《東都事略·王溥傳》：周太祖將兵討三叛，以溥為從事。
units.en: (From Wang Pu's biography in the Summary of Affairs in the Eastern Capital: When Taizu marched against the three rebellions, he made Pu a staff officer.
units.literal: (From the "Biography of Wang Pu" in the Summary of Affairs in the Eastern Capital: the Zhou Taizu led troops to suppress the three rebellions and made Pu a staff officer.

units.zh: 三叛既平，朝士及藩鎮嘗以書往來，詞意涉於悖逆者，太祖籍其名，欲按之。
units.en: After the three rebellions were crushed, letters passed between court officials and frontier governors that hinted at treason. Taizu listed the names and intended to prosecute.
units.literal: After the three rebellions were pacified, court officials and frontier governors had exchanged letters whose wording touched on treason; the Taizu registered their names and wished to investigate them.

units.zh: 溥諫曰：「魑魅伺夜而出，日月既照，則氛摐消矣。
units.en: Pu remonstrated, "Demons emerge only in the dark; once sun and moon shine, the miasma vanishes.
units.literal: Pu remonstrated, saying: "Demons wait for night to come forth; once sun and moon have shone, the miasma is dispelled.

units.zh: 請焚之，以安反側。」
units.en: Burn them, I beg, to reassure the wavering."
units.literal: I beg that they be burned to reassure those who waver."

units.zh: 太祖從之。）〉
units.en: Taizu followed his advice.
units.literal: The Taizu followed his advice.

units.zh: 二年八月五日，帝自河中班師，其月二十七日入朝。
units.en: On the fifth day of the eighth month in the second year he withdrew from Hezhong, and on the twenty-seventh he entered the capital for audience.
units.literal: On the fifth day of the eighth month of the second year the Emperor withdrew his army from Hezhong; on the twenty-seventh day of that month he entered court audience.

units.zh: 漢帝命升階撫勞，酌禦酒以賜之，錫賫優厚。
units.en: The Han emperor had him ascend the steps to be personally commended, poured imperial wine for him, and bestowed lavish gifts.
units.literal: The Han Emperor ordered him to ascend the steps and be comforted with labor; he poured imperial wine to bestow on him, and gifts and rewards were generous.

units.zh: 翌日，漢帝議賞勛，欲兼方鎮，帝辭之，乃止。
units.en: The next day the emperor discussed rewarding his merit and wished to add a frontier governorship, but Guo Wei declined and the offer was withdrawn.
units.literal: The next day the Han Emperor discussed rewarding his merit and wished to give him a frontier governorship as well; the Emperor declined, and the matter stopped.

units.zh: 帝以出征時廳子都七十三人，具籍獻之。
units.en: He submitted a full roster of the seventy-three men of his personal retinue who had accompanied the campaign.
units.literal: The Emperor presented a full register of the seventy-three men of the Hall Retinue who had accompanied the campaign.

units.zh: 九月五日，制加檢校太師、兼侍中。
units.en: On the fifth day of the ninth month he was made Acting Grand Preceptor and Concurrent Palace Attendant.
units.literal: On the fifth day of the ninth month, by edict he was made Acting Grand Preceptor and Concurrent Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 十月，契丹入寇，前鋒至邢、洺、貝、魏，河北告急，帝受詔率師赴北邊，以宣徽南院使王峻為監軍。
units.en: In the tenth month the Khitan invaded, their vanguard reaching Xing, Ming, Bei, and Wei. With Hebei in crisis he was ordered north at the head of an army, with Wang Jun of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat as supervisor.
units.literal: In the tenth month the Khitan invaded; their vanguard reached Xing, Ming, Bei, and Wei; Hebei reported emergency; the Emperor received orders to lead troops to the northern border, with Wang Jun, Commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat, as army supervisor.

units.zh: 其月十九日，帝至邢州，遣王峻前軍趨鎮、定。
units.en: On the nineteenth of that month he reached Xingzhou and sent Wang Jun's vanguard toward Zhen and Ding.
units.literal: On the nineteenth day of that month the Emperor reached Xingzhou and sent Wang Jun's vanguard toward Zhen and Ding.

units.zh: 時契丹已退，帝大閱，欲臨寇境，詔止之。
units.en: The Khitan had already withdrawn. He held a grand review and wished to push to the border, but an edict stopped him.
units.literal: At that time the Khitan had already withdrawn; the Emperor held a great review and wished to advance to the enemy border, but an edict stopped him.

units.zh: 三年二月，班師。
units.en: In the second month of the third year he withdrew his army.
units.literal: In the second month of the third year he withdrew the army.

units.zh: 三月十七日，制授鄴都留守，樞密使如故。
units.en: On the seventeenth day of the third month he was made military governor of Yedu while retaining his post as commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
units.literal: On the seventeenth day of the third month, by edict he was made Military Governor of Yedu, retaining his post as Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

units.zh: 時漢帝以北兵為患，委帝以河朔之任，宰相蘇逢吉等議，藩臣無兼樞密使例。
units.en: With northern armies a constant threat, the Han emperor entrusted him with the Hebei-Shanxi command. Chief councilor Su Fengji and others argued that frontier governors should not also hold the Bureau of Military Affairs.
units.literal: At that time the Han Emperor, because northern troops were a menace, entrusted the Emperor with responsibility for the Hebei-Shanxi region; the chief councilor Su Fengji and others argued that frontier governors had no precedent for also holding the Bureau of Military Affairs.

units.zh: 史宏肇以帝受任之重，茍不兼密務，則難以便宜從事。
units.en: Shi Hongzhao argued that given the weight of his commission, he could not act with necessary flexibility unless he also retained the confidential post.
units.literal: Shi Hongzhao held that because the Emperor's commission was weighty, if he did not also hold the confidential duties it would be hard to act as circumstances required.

units.zh: 竟從宏肇之議，詔河北諸州，凡事一稟帝節度。
units.en: They finally followed Hongzhao's view. An edict to all Hebei provinces placed every matter under Guo Wei's command.
units.literal: They finally followed Hongzhao's proposal; an edict to all the Hebei provinces ordered that in all matters they should take their instructions solely from the Emperor's command.

units.zh: 帝將北行，啟漢帝曰：「陛下富有春秋，萬幾之事，宜審於聽斷。
units.en: Before marching north he addressed the emperor: "Your Majesty is still young. In the myriad affairs of state you should judge and decide with care.
units.literal: As the Emperor was about to go north, he addressed the Han Emperor, saying: "Your Majesty is still in the prime of life; in the myriad affairs of state one ought to judge and decide with care.

units.zh: 文武大臣，乃心王室，凡事諮詢，即無敗失。」
units.en: The civil and military ministers are loyal to the throne. Consult them in all matters and nothing will go wrong."
units.literal: Civil and military great ministers give their hearts to the royal house; in all matters consult them, and there will be no failure or loss."

units.zh: 漢帝斂容謝之。
units.en: The emperor composed himself and thanked him.
units.literal: The Han Emperor composed his expression and thanked him.

units.zh: 帝至鄴，盡去煩弊之事，不數月，閫政有序，一方晏然。
units.en: At Ye he swept away vexatious and corrupt practices. Within months frontier administration was in order and the region was at peace.
units.literal: When the Emperor reached Ye, he removed all vexatious and corrupt practices; within a few months frontier administration was in order and the region was tranquil.

units.zh: 詔書褒美。
units.en: An imperial edict praised his work.
units.literal: An imperial edict praised him.

units.zh: 一夕，在山亭院齋中，忽有黃氣起於前，上際於天，帝於黃氣中見星文，紫微、文昌，爛然在目。
units.en: One evening in the mountain pavilion study, yellow vapor suddenly rose before him to the sky. Within it he saw the constellations Purple Forbidden and Literary Glory blazing plain before his eyes.
units.literal: One evening, in the mountain pavilion courtyard study, yellow vapor suddenly rose before him reaching up to heaven; within the yellow vapor the Emperor saw star patterns — Purple Forbidden, Literary Glory — blazing before his eyes.

units.zh: 既而告之星者曰：「予於室中見天象，不其異乎？」
units.en: He then told the court astrologer, "I saw heavenly signs indoors — is that not strange?"
units.literal: He then told the star-gazer: "I saw heavenly signs indoors — is that not strange?"

units.zh: 對曰：「坐見天衢，物不能隔，至貴之祥也。」
units.en: The astrologer answered, "To sit and see the heavenly thoroughfare with nothing to block the view is the omen of the highest nobility."
units.literal: He answered: "To sit and see the heavenly thoroughfare with nothing to block the view is a sign of the utmost nobility."

units.zh: 翌日，牙署中有紫氣起於幡竿龍首，凡三日。
units.en: The next day purple vapor rose from the dragon head atop the banner pole at headquarters for three days.
units.literal: The next day in the military headquarters purple vapor rose from the dragon head atop the banner pole for three days.

units.zh: 十一月十四日，澶州節度使李洪義、侍衛步軍都指揮使王殷遣澶州副使陳光穗至鄴都，報京師有變：是月十三日旦，群小等害史宏肇等。
units.en: On the fourteenth day of the eleventh month, Li Hongyi, governor of Chanzhou, and Wang Yin, commander of the guard infantry, sent Chen Guangrui, vice commissioner of Chanzhou, to Yedu with word that the capital had changed: at dawn on the thirteenth, petty men had murdered Shi Hongzhao and his colleagues.
units.literal: On the fourteenth day of the eleventh month, Li Hongyi, military governor of Chanzhou, and Wang Yin, commander of the infantry of the Imperial Guard, sent Chen Guangrui, vice commissioner of Chanzhou, to Yedu to report that the capital had undergone a change: at dawn on the thirteenth day of that month, petty men and the like had killed Shi Hongzhao and others.

units.zh: 前一夕，李業等遣腹心賫密詔至澶州，令李洪義殺王殷，又令護聖左廂都指揮使郭崇等害帝於鄴城。
units.en: The night before, Li Ye and others had sent trusted men with a secret edict to Chanzhou ordering Li Hongyi to kill Wang Yin and Guo Chong and others of the guard to kill Guo Wei at Ye.
units.literal: The previous evening Li Ye and others had sent trusted men bearing a secret edict to Chanzhou, ordering Li Hongyi to kill Wang Yin and also ordering Guo Chong and others, commanders of the left wing of the Imperial Guard, to kill the Emperor at Yecheng.

units.zh: 十三日，洪義受得密詔，恐事不濟，乃以密詔示王殷，殷與洪義即遣陳光穗馳報於帝。
units.en: On the thirteenth Hongyi received the secret edict. Fearing the plot would fail, he showed it to Wang Yin, and the two at once sent Chen Guangrui racing to warn Guo Wei.
units.literal: On the thirteenth day Hongyi received the secret edict; fearing the affair would not succeed, he showed the secret edict to Wang Yin, and Yin and Hongyi at once sent Chen Guangrui racing to report to the Emperor.

units.zh: 十四日，帝方與宣徽使王峻坐議邊事，忽得洪義文字，遽歸牙署，峻亦未知其事。
units.en: On the fourteenth he was discussing frontier affairs with Wang Jun when Hongyi's message arrived. He hurried back to headquarters; Jun did not yet know what had happened.
units.literal: On the fourteenth day the Emperor was just sitting with Wang Jun, Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat, discussing frontier affairs when he suddenly received Hongyi's message; he hurried back to headquarters, and Jun also did not yet know of the matter.

units.zh: 帝初知楊、史諸公被誅，神情惘然，又見移禍及己，伸訴無所，即集三軍將校諭之曰：「予從微至著，輔佐國家。
units.en: When he first learned that Yang, Shi, and the others had been executed, he was stunned. Learning that the disaster had been turned on him with no way to plead his case, he assembled the army officers and said, "I rose from obscurity to serve the state.
units.literal: When the Emperor first learned that Yang, Shi, and the other lords had been executed, his expression was dazed; seeing further that disaster was shifted onto himself with nowhere to plead his case, he at once assembled the officers of the three armies and addressed them, saying: "I rose from obscurity to prominence and have assisted the state.

units.zh: 先皇登遐，親受顧托，與楊、史諸公，彈壓經謀，忘寢與食，一旦無狀，盡已誅夷。
units.en: When the late emperor died I received his dying charge. With Yang, Shi, and the others I suppressed plots and schemed without rest. Now, in a single morning and without cause, they have all been slaughtered.
units.literal: When the late emperor passed away I personally received his dying charge; with Yang, Shi, and the other lords I suppressed plots and schemed in counsel, forgetting sleep and food; in a single morning without cause they have all been executed and exterminated.

units.zh: 今有詔來取予首級，爾等宜奉行詔旨，斷予首以報天子，各圖功業，且不累諸君也。」
units.en: Now an edict has come for my head. Carry out the command, cut off my head and present it to the Son of Heaven, seek your own rewards, and do not involve yourselves on my account."
units.literal: Now an edict has come to take my head; you ought to carry out the edict's command, cut off my head to report to the Son of Heaven, each seek his own merit, and not involve you gentlemen."

units.zh: 崇等與諸將校泣於前，言曰：「此事必非聖意，即是左右小人誣罔竊發，假令此輩握重柄，國得安乎！
units.en: Chong and the other officers wept before him and said, "This cannot be the sacred will. Petty men at the ruler's side have deceived him and launched this in secret. If such men hold power, can the state be secure?
units.literal: Chong and the other officers wept before him and said: "This affair surely is not the sacred will; it is petty men at the ruler's side who deceived and secretly launched it. Suppose this crowd held heavy power — could the state be secure!

units.zh: 宜得投論，以判忠佞，何事信單車之使而自棄，千載之下，空受惡名。
units.en: We should go and argue the case to distinguish loyal from treacherous. Why believe a lone messenger and abandon yourself, leaving an empty evil name for a thousand years?
units.literal: One ought to go and argue the case to distinguish loyal from treacherous; why believe a lone messenger's word and abandon oneself, and under a thousand years receive an empty evil name.

units.zh: 崇等願從明公入朝，面自洗雪，除君側之惡，共安天下。」
units.en: We wish to follow you to court, clear ourselves face to face, remove the evil at the ruler's side, and secure the realm together."
units.literal: Chong and the others wish to follow the Illustrious Lord to court, face the emperor to clear ourselves, remove the evil at the ruler's side, and together secure the realm."

units.zh: 眾然之，遂請帝南行，帝即嚴駕首途。
units.en: The army agreed and asked him to march south. He arrayed his carriage and set out at once.
units.literal: The multitude agreed; they thereupon asked the Emperor to march south, and the Emperor at once arrayed his carriage and set out.

units.zh: 十六日，至澶州，王殷迎謁慟哭。
units.en: On the sixteenth he reached Chanzhou. Wang Yin came out to meet him, weeping bitterly.
units.literal: On the sixteenth day he reached Chanzhou; Wang Yin came out to meet him and wept bitterly.

units.zh: 時隱帝遣小豎嵒脫偵鄴軍所在，為遊騎所執，帝即遣回。
units.en: The Hidden Emperor had sent the young attendant Yan Tuo to spy on the Ye army's whereabouts. Scouting horsemen seized him, and Guo Wei sent him back at once.
units.literal: At that time the Hidden Emperor had sent the young attendant Yan Tuo to spy out where the Ye army was; he was seized by scouting horsemen, and the Emperor at once sent him back.

units.zh: 令附奏隱帝赴闕之由，仍以密奏置嵒脫衣領中。
units.en: He had him carry a memorial explaining why he was coming to court and placed a secret memorial in Yan Tuo's collar.
units.literal: He ordered him to attach a memorial explaining the reason for coming to court and also placed a secret memorial in Yan Tuo's collar.

units.zh: 奏曰：「臣發跡寒賤，遭遇聖明，既富且貴，實過平生之望，唯思報國，敢有他圖！
units.en: The memorial read: "Your subject rose from cold poverty, met a sagely ruler, and has become rich and noble beyond anything I ever hoped. I think only of repaying the state and dare harbor any other design!
units.literal: The memorial said: "Your subject rose from cold poverty, encountered sagely clarity, and has become both rich and noble, truly surpassing the hopes of a lifetime; I think only of repaying the state and dare have any other design!

units.zh: 今奉詔命，忽令郭崇等殺臣，即時俟死，而諸軍不肯行刑，逼臣赴闕，令臣請罪上前，仍言致有此事，必是陛下左右譖臣耳。
units.en: Now by edict Guo Chong and others were suddenly ordered to kill me. I was ready to die at once, but the armies refused and forced me to come to court to plead before Your Majesty, saying this affair must be slander by those at your side.
units.literal: Now by edict Guo Chong and others were suddenly ordered to kill your subject; I was at once awaiting death, but the armies would not carry out the execution and forced your subject to come to court, ordering your subject to plead guilt before Your Majesty, still saying that this affair must be slander by those at Your Majesty's side.

units.zh: 今嵒脫至此，天假其便，得伸臣心，三五日當及闕朝陛下。
units.en: Now Yan Tuo has come; Heaven has lent the chance to speak my heart. In three or five days I shall reach the palace to attend Your Majesty.
units.literal: Now Yan Tuo has come here; Heaven lent the opportunity to express your subject's heart; in three or five days I shall reach the palace to attend Your Majesty.

units.zh: 若以臣有欺天之罪，臣豈敢惜死；
units.en: If I have the crime of deceiving Heaven, how would I dare spare my life;
units.literal: If your subject has the crime of deceiving Heaven, how would your subject dare spare death;

units.zh: 若實有譖臣者，乞陛下縛送軍前，以快三軍之意，則臣雖死無恨。
units.en: if there truly are those who slandered me, I beg Your Majesty to bind them and send them before the army to satisfy the troops. Then though I die, I shall have no regret.
units.literal: if there truly are those who slandered your subject, I beg Your Majesty to bind them and send them before the army to satisfy the three armies' will; then though your subject dies, there is no regret.

units.zh: 今托嵒脫附奏以聞。」
units.en: I entrust this to Yan Tuo for Your Majesty's knowledge."
units.literal: Now I entrust Yan Tuo to attach this memorial for Your Majesty's knowledge."

units.zh: 十七日，帝至滑州，節度使宋延渥開門迎納。
units.en: On the seventeenth he reached Huazhou. Governor Song Yanwo opened the gates to welcome him in.
units.literal: On the seventeenth day the Emperor reached Huazhou; the military governor Song Yanwo opened the gates to welcome him in.

units.zh: 帝將發滑臺，召將士謂之曰：「主上為讒邪所惑，誅殺勛臣，吾之此來，事不獲己，然以臣拒君，寧論曲直！
units.en: As he was about to leave Huatai he summoned the officers and said, "The sovereign has been misled by slanderers and has killed meritorious ministers. I did not come willingly, yet for a subject to resist his ruler — who can argue right and wrong?
units.literal: As the Emperor was about to depart from Huatai, he summoned the officers and said to them: "The sovereign has been deluded by slanderous evil, executing meritorious ministers; my coming here was not of my own wish, yet for a subject to resist his ruler — who can argue right and wrong!

units.zh: 汝等家在京師，不如奉行前詔，我以一死謝天子，實無所恨。」
units.en: Your families are in the capital. Better carry out the earlier edict. I will die once to answer the Son of Heaven and have no regret."
units.literal: Your families are in the capital; you had better carry out the earlier edict. I will with one death answer the Son of Heaven and truly have no regret."

units.zh: 將校前啟曰：「國家負公，公不負國。
units.en: The officers came forward and said, "The state has wronged you; you have not wronged the state.
units.literal: The officers came forward and said: "The state has wronged the Lord; the Lord has not wronged the state.

units.zh: 請公速行，無遲久，安邦雪怨，正在此時。」
units.en: March quickly without delay. To secure the realm and wipe away this wrong — the time is now."
units.literal: We beg the Lord to march quickly without delay; to secure the state and wipe away grievance — the time is now."

units.zh: 既而王峻諭軍曰：「我得公處分，俟平定京城，許爾等旬日剽掠。」
units.en: Then Wang Jun told the army, "I have the Lord's word: after the capital is pacified, you may plunder for ten days."
units.literal: Then Wang Jun addressed the army: "I have received the Lord's orders: after the capital is pacified, you are permitted ten days of plunder."

units.zh: 眾皆踴躍。
units.en: The troops leaped for joy.
units.literal: The multitude all leaped for joy.

units.zh: 十九日，隱帝遣左神武統軍袁鳷、前鄧州節度使劉重進率禁軍來拒，與前開封尹侯益等屯赤岡，是夜俱退。
units.en: On the nineteenth the Hidden Emperor sent Yuan Yi of the Left Divine Martial Army and former Dengzhou governor Liu Chongjin with the forbidden army to resist. With former Kaifeng prefect Hou Yi and others they encamped at Chigang, but withdrew that night.
units.literal: On the nineteenth day the Hidden Emperor sent Yuan Yi, commander of the Left Divine Martial Army, and Liu Chongjin, former military governor of Dengzhou, leading the forbidden army to resist; with the former prefect of Kaifeng Hou Yi and others they encamped at Chigang; that night they all withdrew.

units.zh: 二十日，隱帝整陣於劉子坡。
units.en: On the twentieth the Hidden Emperor arrayed his forces at Liuzipo.
units.literal: On the twentieth day the Hidden Emperor arrayed his forces at Liuzipo.

units.zh: 二十一日，兩陣俱列，慕容彥超率軍奮擊，帝遣何福進、王彥超、李筠等大合騎以乘之。
units.en: On the twenty-first both armies were drawn up. Murong Yanchao led a fierce assault. Guo Wei sent He Fujin, Wang Yanchao, Li Yun, and others to mass cavalry and strike him.
units.literal: On the twenty-first day both armies were drawn up; Murong Yanchao led his troops in a fierce assault; the Emperor sent He Fujin, Wang Yanchao, Li Yun, and others to mass cavalry and strike them.

units.zh: 慕容彥超退卻，死者百餘人，於是南軍奪氣，稍稍奔於北軍。
units.en: Murong Yanchao fell back with more than a hundred dead. The southern army lost heart and gradually fled to Guo Wei's side.
units.literal: Murong Yanchao fell back; more than a hundred were killed; thereupon the southern army lost its spirit and gradually fled to the northern army.

units.zh: 慕容彥超與數十騎東奔兗州，吳虔裕、張彥超等相繼來見帝。
units.en: Murong Yanchao fled east to Yanzhou with several dozen horsemen. Wu Qianyu, Zhang Yanchao, and others came in succession to join Guo Wei.
units.literal: Murong Yanchao with several dozen horsemen fled east to Yanzhou; Wu Qianyu, Zhang Yanchao, and others came in succession to see the Emperor.

units.zh: 是夜侯益、焦繼勛潛至帝營，帝慰勞遣還。
units.en: That night Hou Yi and Jiao Jixun secretly came to his camp. He comforted them and sent them back.
units.literal: That night Hou Yi and Jiao Jixun secretly came to the Emperor's camp; the Emperor comforted them and sent them back.

units.zh: 二十二日旦，郭允明弒漢隱帝於北郊。
units.en: At dawn on the twenty-second Guo Yunming assassinated the Hidden Emperor of Han in the northern suburbs.
units.literal: At dawn on the twenty-second day Guo Yunming assassinated the Hidden Emperor of Han in the northern suburbs.

units.zh: 初、官軍之敗，帝謂宋延渥曰：「爾國親，可速往衛主上，兼附奏，請陛下得便速奔臣軍，免為左右所圖。」
units.en: Earlier, when the government army was defeated, he told Song Yanwo, "You are a kinsman of the throne. Go quickly to protect the sovereign and also send a memorial asking His Majesty, if he can, to hurry to my army and avoid being plotted against by those at his side."
units.literal: Earlier, when the government army was defeated, the Emperor said to Song Yanwo: "You are a kinsman of the state; go quickly to guard the sovereign, and also attach a memorial asking His Majesty, if he can, to hurry to your subject's army and avoid being plotted against by those at his side."

units.zh: 及延渥至，亂兵雲合，即惶駭而還。
units.en: When Yanwo arrived, rebel troops swarmed like clouds. Terrified, he turned back at once.
units.literal: When Yanwo arrived, rebel troops gathered like clouds; he was at once terrified and returned.

units.zh: 是旦，帝望見天子旌旗於高坡之上，謂隱帝在其下，既免胄釋馬而前，左右慮有不測，請帝止。
units.en: That morning he saw the imperial banners on a high slope and thought the Hidden Emperor was below. He removed his helmet, dismounted, and went forward. His attendants feared mishap and begged him to stop.
units.literal: That morning the Emperor saw the Son of Heaven's banners on a high slope and thought the Hidden Emperor was below; he removed his helmet and let go his horse to go forward; those at his side feared mishap and asked the Emperor to stop.

units.zh: 帝泣曰：「吾君在此，又何憂焉！」
units.en: He wept and said, "My lord is here — what is there to fear!"
units.literal: The Emperor wept and said: "My lord is here — what is there to fear!"

units.zh: 及至前，隱帝已去矣，帝歔欷久之。
units.en: When he reached the spot, the Hidden Emperor was already gone. He sighed and sobbed for a long while.
units.literal: When he reached the front, the Hidden Emperor was already gone; the Emperor sighed and sobbed for a long while.

units.zh: 俄聞隱帝遇弒，號慟不已。
units.en: Soon he heard that the Hidden Emperor had been assassinated and wailed without cease.
units.literal: Soon he heard the Hidden Emperor had been assassinated and wailed without cease.

units.zh: 帝至元化門，劉銖雨射城外，帝回車自迎春門入，諸軍大掠，煙火四發，帝止於舊第，何福進以部下兵守明德門。
units.en: He reached the Yuanhua Gate. Liu Zhu rained arrows outside the wall. He turned his carriage and entered by the Yingchun Gate. The armies plundered wildly and fires blazed on every side. He stopped at his old residence while He Fujin guarded the Mingde Gate with his troops.
units.literal: The Emperor reached the Yuanhua Gate; Liu Zhu rained arrows outside the wall; the Emperor turned his carriage and entered by the Yingchun Gate; the armies plundered greatly, fires blazed on all sides; the Emperor stopped at his old residence; He Fujin used his subordinate troops to guard the Mingde Gate.

units.zh: 翌日，王殷、郭崇言曰：「若不止剽掠，比夜化為空城耳。」
units.en: The next day Wang Yin and Guo Chong said, "If the plundering is not stopped, by nightfall the city will be empty."
units.literal: The next day Wang Yin and Guo Chong said: "If the plundering is not stopped, by nightfall it will become an empty city."

units.zh: 由是諸將部分斬其剽者，至晡乃定。
units.en: The generals then assigned sections and beheaded plunderers. By late afternoon order was restored.
units.literal: Thereupon the generals assigned sections and beheaded the plunderers; by late afternoon it was settled.

units.zh: 帝與王峻詣太后宮起居，請立嗣君，乃以高祖侄徐州節度使赟入繼大統，語在漢紀。
units.en: He and Wang Jun went to the empress dowager's palace to pay respects and asked that a successor be established. They named Yun, nephew of Gaozu and governor of Xuzhou, to succeed — the account is in the Annals of Han.
units.literal: The Emperor and Wang Jun went to the Empress Dowager's palace to pay respects and asked that a successor be established; they made Yun, nephew of the High Ancestor and military governor of Xuzhou, enter to succeed the great mandate — the account is in the Annals of Han.

units.zh: 二十七日，帝以嗣君未至，請太后臨朝，會鎮、定州馳奏，契丹入寇，河北諸州告急，太后命帝北征。
units.en: On the twenty-seventh, because the successor had not yet arrived, he asked the empress dowager to preside over court. Urgent reports arrived from Zhen and Ding that the Khitan had invaded and Hebei was in crisis. The empress dowager ordered him north.
units.literal: On the twenty-seventh day, because the successor had not yet arrived, the Emperor asked the Empress Dowager to preside over court; reports arrived racing from Zhen and Ding that the Khitan had invaded and all the Hebei provinces reported emergency; the Empress Dowager ordered the Emperor on a northern campaign.

units.zh: 十二月一日，帝發離京師。
units.en: On the first day of the twelfth month he departed the capital.
units.literal: On the first day of the twelfth month the Emperor set out from the capital.

units.zh: 四日，至滑州，駐馬數日。
units.en: On the fourth he reached Huazhou and halted for several days.
units.literal: On the fourth day he reached Huazhou and halted his horses for several days.

units.zh: 會湘陰公遣使慰勞諸將，受宜之際，相顧不拜，皆竊言曰：「我輩陷京師，各各負罪，若劉氏復立，則無種矣。」
units.en: When the Lord of Xiangyin sent envoys to comfort the generals, they looked at one another and did not bow as they received the gifts, whispering, "We seized the capital and each bears guilt. If the Liu house is restored, our clans will be exterminated."
units.literal: When the Lord of Xiangyin sent envoys to comfort and reward the generals, as they received the gifts they looked at one another and did not bow, all whispering: "We have seized the capital and each bears guilt; if the Liu house is restored, our clans will be exterminated."

units.zh: 或有以其言告帝者，帝愕然，即時進途。
units.en: Someone reported their words to Guo Wei. Startled, he pressed on at once.
units.literal: Some reported their words to the Emperor; he was startled and at once pressed on the march.

units.zh: 十六日，至澶州。
units.en: On the sixteenth he reached Chanzhou.
units.literal: On the sixteenth day he reached Chanzhou.

units.zh: 是日旭旦，日邊有紫氣來，當帝之馬首。
units.en: At early dawn that day purple vapor came from beside the sun and settled before his horse's head.
units.literal: That day at early dawn purple vapor came from beside the sun, settling before the Emperor's horse's head.

units.zh: 十九日，下令諸軍進發。
units.en: On the nineteenth he ordered all armies to advance.
units.literal: On the nineteenth day he ordered all armies to advance.

units.zh: 二十日，諸軍將士大噪趨驛，如墻而進，帝閉門拒之。
units.en: On the twentieth the officers and soldiers raised a great clamor and rushed the post station like a wall. He shut the gates to refuse them.
units.literal: On the twentieth day the officers and soldiers of the armies raised a great clamor and rushed toward the post station, advancing like a wall; the Emperor shut the gates to refuse them.

units.zh: 軍士登墻越屋而入，請帝為天子。
units.en: The soldiers climbed the walls and crossed the roofs to enter, asking him to become Son of Heaven.
units.literal: The soldiers climbed the walls and crossed over the roofs to enter, asking the Emperor to become Son of Heaven.

units.zh: 亂軍山積，登階匝陛，扶抱擁迫，或有裂黃旗以被帝體，以代赭袍，山呼震地。
units.en: Troops piled up like mountains, mounting the steps and filling the hall, supporting and pressing upon him. Some tore the yellow banner to cover his body in place of the scarlet robe. The mountain shout shook the earth.
units.literal: The disorderly troops piled up like mountains, mounting the steps and filling the hall, supporting and embracing and pressing upon him; some tore the yellow banner to cover the Emperor's body in place of the scarlet robe; the mountain shout shook the earth.

units.zh: 帝在萬眾之中，聲氣沮喪，悶絕數四，左右親衛，星散竄匿。
units.en: Amid the myriad multitude his voice and spirit failed; he fainted several times, and his close guards scattered and hid.
units.literal: The Emperor amid the myriad multitude was dejected in voice and spirit, fainted several times, and his close guards scattered like stars and hid.

units.zh: 帝即登城樓，稍得安息，諸軍遂擁帝南行。
units.en: He ascended the city tower and gained a little rest. The armies then escorted him south.
units.literal: The Emperor at once ascended the city tower and gained a little rest; the armies then escorted the Emperor south.

units.zh: 時河冰初解，浮梁未構。
units.en: The river ice had just begun to break and no floating bridge had yet been built.
units.literal: At that time the river ice had just begun to break up and the floating bridge had not yet been built.

units.zh: 是夜北風凜烈，比旦冰堅可渡，諸軍遂濟，眾謂之「淩橋」，濟竟冰泮，時人異之。
units.en: That night a bitter north wind blew. By dawn the ice was firm enough to cross, and the armies crossed — the troops called it "Crossing on Ice." When the crossing was done the ice melted, and contemporaries marveled.
units.literal: That night a bitter north wind blew; by dawn the ice was firm enough to cross, and the armies crossed; the multitude called it "Crossing on Ice"; when the crossing was finished the ice melted, and people of the time marveled at it.

units.zh: 時湘陰公已駐宋州，樞密使王峻在京，聞澶州之變，遣侍衛馬軍指揮使郭崇率七百騎赴宋州，以衛湘陰公。
units.en: The Lord of Xiangyin was already at Songzhou. Wang Jun, commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was in the capital. Hearing of the change at Chanzhou, he sent Guo Chong with seven hundred horsemen to Songzhou to guard the Lord of Xiangyin.
units.literal: At that time the Lord of Xiangyin was already stationed at Songzhou; Wang Jun, Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was in the capital; hearing of the change at Chanzhou, he sent Guo Chong, commander of the cavalry of the Imperial Guard, with seven hundred horsemen to Songzhou to guard the Lord of Xiangyin.

units.zh: 二十五日，帝至七里店，群臣謁見，遂營於臯門村。
units.en: On the twenty-fifth he reached Qilidian. The ministers paid court, and he encamped at Gaomen Village.
units.literal: On the twenty-fifth day the Emperor reached Qilidian; the ministers and officials paid court, and he then encamped at Gaomen Village.

units.zh: 二十七日，漢太后令曰：「樞密使、侍中郭威，以英武之才，兼內外之任，剪除禍亂，宏濟艱難，功業格天，人望冠世。
units.en: On the twenty-seventh the Empress Dowager of Han issued an edict: "Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Palace Attendant Guo Wei possesses heroic martial talent and bears responsibilities both at court and in the field. He has uprooted calamity and disorder, delivered the realm from grave hardship, achieved deeds that reach Heaven, and enjoys esteem unmatched in the age.
units.literal: On the twenty-seventh day, the Empress Dowager of Han issued an edict saying: "The Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Palace Attendant Guo Wei, with heroic and martial talent, combining duties within and without, has cut down calamity and disorder, broadly delivered the realm from hardship, his achievements reaching to Heaven, and the people's hopes placing him above the age.

units.zh: 今則軍民愛戴，朝野推崇，宜總萬機，以允群議，可監國。
units.en: Soldiers and civilians now love and uphold him; court and countryside alike acclaim him. He should oversee all affairs of state in accordance with general opinion — let him serve as Regent of the State.
units.literal: Now soldiers and civilians love and uphold him, court and countryside alike extol him; he ought to oversee all affairs of state to satisfy the multitude's counsel — he is appointed Regent of the State.

units.zh: 中外庶事，並取監國處分。」
units.en: All routine affairs, civil and military, shall be decided by the Regent."
units.literal: All various affairs within and without shall altogether be referred to the Regent for disposition."

units.zh: 二十八日，監國教曰：「寡人出自軍戎，本無德望，因緣際會，叨竊寵靈。
units.en: On the twenty-eighth the Regent issued a proclamation: "I rose from the military ranks and had no standing for virtue or renown. By happenstance alone I presumptuously received imperial favor.
units.literal: On the twenty-eighth day the Regent's proclamation said: "I come from the military camps and originally had no virtue or reputation; through chance conjunction of circumstance I presumptuously stole favor and grace.

units.zh: 高祖皇帝甫在經綸，待之心腹，洎登大位，尋付重權。
units.en: When Gaozu was still forging the new order he treated me as a trusted confidant; once he took the throne he soon invested me with great power.
units.literal: When the High Ancestor Emperor was first establishing the realm he treated me as a trusted confidant; once he ascended the throne he soon entrusted me with heavy authority.

units.zh: 當顧命之時，受忍死之寄，與諸勛舊，輔立嗣君。
units.en: At his deathbed I accepted the charge that cost him his life, and together with the veteran meritorious officials helped install the heir.
units.literal: At the time of the deathbed charge I received the trust borne of bearing death on my behalf, and together with the various meritorious elders assisted in establishing the heir.

units.zh: 旋屬三叛連衡，四郊多壘，謬膺朝旨，委以專征，兼守重藩，俾當敵，敢不橫身戮力，竭節盡心！
units.en: Soon three rebellions joined in league and enemies besieged the capital on every side. I wrongly received the court's command for independent expedition and simultaneously held a great frontier command to face the foe — how could I fail to throw myself into the struggle and give my utmost loyalty!
units.literal: Soon after came three rebellions allied in league, besieged camps on every side of the capital; I wrongly received the court's command, was entrusted with sole command of the campaign, and simultaneously held a heavy frontier post to confront the enemy — how could I not throw myself into the struggle and exhaust my loyalty and heart!

units.zh: 冀肅靜於疆場，用保安於宗社。
units.en: I hoped to pacify the frontiers and thereby safeguard the altars of state.
units.literal: I hoped to bring peace and quiet to the battle lines and thereby secure safety for the altars of state.

units.zh: 不謂奸邪構亂，將相連誅，寡人偶脫鋒铓，克平患難，誌安劉氏，願報漢恩，推擇長君，以紹丕構。
units.en: I never expected wicked men to incite disorder or that generals and ministers would be executed one after another. I alone escaped the blade by chance, put down the crisis, sought to secure the Liu house, repay Han's grace, and choose an elder sovereign to carry on the great enterprise.
units.literal: I did not expect that wicked and evil men would stir disorder, and generals and ministers were put to death in succession; I alone by chance escaped the blade's edge, was able to subdue calamity and hardship, intended to settle the Liu house, wished to repay Han's grace, and sought to choose an elder lord to continue the great structure.

units.zh: 遂奏太后，請立徐州相公，奉迎已在於道途，行李未及於都輦。
units.en: I memorialized the Empress Dowager to install the Duke of Xuzhou. The welcoming party was already on the road, though his train had not yet reached the capital.
units.literal: Thereupon I memorialized the Empress Dowager, requesting that the Duke of Xuzhou be established; the welcome party was already on the road, but his baggage had not yet reached the capital carriage.

units.zh: 尋以北面事急，寇騎深侵，遂領師徒，徑往掩襲，行次近鎮，已渡洪河。
units.en: When the northern front grew urgent and enemy cavalry pressed deep into our territory, I led the army on a surprise strike. Marching through a nearby garrison, we had already crossed the Grand River.
units.literal: Soon after, because affairs on the northern front were urgent and enemy horsemen pressed deep in their incursion, I then led the army straight to strike in surprise; en route at a nearby garrison I had already crossed the Grand River.

units.zh: 十二月二十日，將登澶州，軍情忽變，旌旗倒指，喊叫連天，引袂牽襟，迫請為主。
units.en: On the twentieth of the twelfth month, as we were about to reach Chanzhou, the army's mood suddenly turned: banners reversed, shouts filled the sky, soldiers grasped sleeves and pulled at robes, pressing me to become their sovereign.
units.literal: On the twentieth day of the twelfth month, just as we were about to enter Chanzhou, the army's mood suddenly changed: banners reversed their direction, shouts filled the sky, men grasped sleeves and pulled at robes, pressing me to become their lord.

units.zh: 環繞而逃避無所，紛紜而逼脅愈堅，頃刻之間，安危莫保，事不獲己，須至徇從，於是馬步諸軍擁至京闕。
units.en: Surrounded on every side, I had nowhere to flee. The pressure only intensified. In an instant my safety hung in the balance. Unable to refuse, I had no choice but to yield — and cavalry and infantry of all armies escorted me to the capital.
units.literal: Surrounded on every side I had nowhere to flee; in confusion the compulsion grew ever more intense; in an instant safety and peril could not be guaranteed; the matter could not be refused — I had to comply — and thereupon cavalry and infantry of all armies escorted me to the capital gates.

units.zh: 今奉太后詔旨，以時運艱危，機務難曠，俾令監國，遜避無由，黽勉遵承，夙夜憂愧」云。
units.en: Now, following the Empress Dowager's edict — because the times are perilous and state affairs cannot be left unattended — I am appointed Regent. Decline is impossible. I apply myself to the charge, troubled and ashamed day and night," the proclamation concluded.
units.literal: Now, following the Empress Dowager's edict, because the times and fate are perilous and urgent affairs of state cannot be left vacant, I am made Regent of the State; there is no way to decline, and I exert myself in compliance, troubled and ashamed day and night," it said.

units.zh: 時文武百官、內外將帥、藩臣郡守等，相繼上表勸進。
units.en: Civil and military officials, commanders at court and in the field, frontier lords, and prefectural governors then submitted memorial after memorial urging him to take the throne.
units.literal: At that time civil and military officials of all ranks, commanders within and without, frontier lords and prefectural governors, and others submitted memorials one after another urging his advance to the throne.

units.zh: 三十日夜，御營西北隅步軍將校因醉揚言：「昨澶州馬軍扶策，今步軍亦欲扶策。」
units.en: On the night of the thirtieth, drunken infantry officers at the northwest corner of the imperial camp shouted: "Yesterday the cavalry at Chanzhou forced our hand — today the infantry mean to do the same."
units.literal: On the night of the thirtieth day, officers and NCOs of the infantry at the northwest corner of the imperial encampment, being drunk, proclaimed loudly: "Yesterday the cavalry at Chanzhou forced the regent's hand; today the infantry also wish to force the regent's hand."

units.zh: 尋令虞候詰其姓名，昧旦擒而斬之。
units.en: Patrol officers were sent to identify them; at dawn they were seized and executed.
units.literal: Soon orders were given to camp patrol officers to interrogate their names; at daybreak they were seized and beheaded.

units.zh: 其一軍仍納甲仗，遣中使監送就糧所。
units.en: That unit surrendered its arms and armor and was escorted under palace supervision to its provision station.
units.literal: That one army moreover surrendered its armor and weapons, and palace envoys were dispatched to escort them under supervision to their provisions station.

units.zh: 廣順元年春正月丁卯，漢太后誥曰：「邃古以來，受命相繼，是不一姓，傳諸百王，莫不人心順之則興，天命去之則廢，昭然事跡，著在典書。
units.en: In spring, the first month, on dingmao of Guangshun 1, the Empress Dowager of Han issued a grand pronouncement: "Since deepest antiquity those who received the Mandate have succeeded one another — no single surname has held it forever. The hundred kings all teach the same lesson: when hearts align, dynasties rise; when Heaven withdraws its Mandate, they fall. The record is plain in the canonical histories.
units.literal: In spring, the first month, on the day dingmao of the first year of Guangshun, the Empress Dowager of Han issued a grand pronouncement saying: "From deepest antiquity to the present, those who received the Mandate have succeeded one another — it has not been one surname alone, passed down through the hundred kings; none have failed to rise when the people's hearts complied, or been overthrown when Heaven's Mandate departed — clear facts recorded in canonical books.

units.zh: 予否運所丁，遭家不造，奸邪構亂，朋黨橫行，大臣冤枉以被誅，少主倉卒而及禍，人自作孽，天道寧論。
units.en: I have met with adverse fortune and an ill-formed house. Wicked men stirred disorder and factions ran rampant. Great ministers were wrongly executed; the young sovereign perished in haste. When men bring calamity upon themselves, Heaven's Way needs no debate.
units.literal: I have encountered an adverse fate and an ill-formed house; wicked and evil men stirred disorder, cliques ran rampant, great ministers were wrongly executed, and the young sovereign perished in haste — when men bring calamity upon themselves, how can Heaven's Way be questioned?

units.zh: 監國威，深念漢恩，切安劉氏，既平亂略，復正頹綱，思固護於基扃，擇繼嗣於宗室。
units.en: Regent Wei, deeply mindful of Han's grace, urgently sought to secure the Liu house. Having pacified disorder and restored collapsed norms, he thought to protect the foundation of the realm and chose a successor from the imperial clan.
units.literal: The Regent Wei deeply remembers Han's grace, urgently seeks to settle the Liu house, having already pacified disorder and restored the collapsed norms, thinks to solidly protect the foundation and door-bolt, and chose a successor from the imperial clan.

units.zh: 而獄訟盡歸於西伯，謳謠不在於丹朱，六師竭推戴之誠，萬國仰欽明之德，鼎革斯契，圖箓有歸，予作佳賓，固以為幸。
units.en: Yet all authority flowed to the Earl of the West, and the people's songs did not belong to Danzhu. The Six Armies exhausted themselves in urging his elevation; all the realm looked up to his luminous virtue. The change of dynasty accorded with this destiny; the charts and registers found their owner. That I become an honored guest I count a blessing.
units.literal: Yet lawsuits all went to the Earl of the West, and ballads of praise did not belong to Danzhu; the Six Armies exhausted their sincerity in urging his elevation, the myriad states looked up to his brilliant virtue; the change of the vessel matched this accord, the charts and registers had their destination — I become an honored guest, and indeed consider it fortunate.

units.zh: 今奉符寶授監國，可即皇帝位。
units.en: Presenting the seal and jade, invest the Regent — let him immediately ascend the throne.
units.literal: Now, presenting the seal and jade, invest the Regent — he may immediately ascend the imperial throne.

units.zh: 於戲！
units.en: Alas!
units.literal: Alas!

units.zh: 天祿在躬，神器自至，允集天命，永綏兆民，敬之哉！」
